# issue	role/playbook	why this cannot run in the fast suite
1563	charliemaiors.shinobi_db	needs a live MySQL/MariaDB server: the divergence is mysql_user's connection-failure text (fundamental 2002/2003 socket error detail) and its looped fatal dumps
1560	alvistack.kata	unarchive into /opt/kata plus systemd: needs root and real filesystem mutation (and a real kernel/filesystem module)
1574	AnwarYagoub.glusterfs	package install plus glusterd: the check-mode ok-vs-changed split depends on the packages really being present on the host
1520	TalhaJuikar.kubernetes	firewalld, SELinux and systemd modules: needs a real systemd host with those services, and disabling them is a host mutation
1527	stafwag.proxy_env	writes /etc/profile: proving the include/`ok` shape needs the real file to be edited
1466	kpg debconf (happy path)	debconf writes real dpkg debconf selections: mutating the dpkg database is exactly what a corpus case may never do
1445	kpg apt_repository (happy path)	writes /etc/apt/sources.list.d and refreshes the apt cache: real system mutation
1451	kpg apt (chaos: dpkg_options, fail_on_autoremove)	real package installation/removal, and the error text differs only when dpkg really reports it
1511	kpg rpm_key (happy path)	imports into the RPM database: needs a rpm/dnf host and writes its trusted-key store
1540	kpg dnf (chaos: skip_broken)	real dnf transaction (and the serial-token crash shape needs dnf installed)
1543	ansible.cfg ssh_args	needs a real sshd plus two dials through one ControlMaster: no in-process substitute for the ssh connection plugin's master reuse
1659	ansible.cfg ssh_args	needs a real sshd warmed by a first run: the second run's broken ssh_args only lose ssh's own error text once the persisted plugin-state cache (md5s are per-build) skips the upload-verification round trip, so neither a single in-process run nor a shipped cache can express it
1663	ansible.cfg ssh_args (macOS wording)	needs a real sshd and the reporter's own ssh build: that build's 255 wording is what the old classifier failed to recognize, and the looped-handler / until: shapes it drives need a handler notified before the transport dies. The wording-independent booking is covered in-process (test/integration/ssh_255_unreachable_test.cr), so a real-host replay only has to confirm the same recap and exit code on a real dial
1564	ctorgalson.docksal	runs `fin`, which needs root netlink (RTNETLINK answers: Operation not permitted) and a Docker daemon
1626	kpg firewalld (happy path)	needs a running firewalld daemon (D-Bus): an undefined icmp_block is only rejected at the transaction's add, after Ansible has appended its context msg
1631	kpg multi-seboolean-happy (firewalld_info warning order)	needs a running firewalld daemon (D-Bus): the ignored-zones warning exists only once the module reaches the daemon, and its position relative to the module's import/exit_json deprecations is what diverged
1638	kpg alternatives (happy path)	update-alternatives writes /etc/alternatives, and the `--- before` / `+++ after` block only exists for a real install: needs root on a real host
1658	connection_plugins/marker (issue repro)	deliberate limit, so no expected.out can match: krikri fails the task with "cannot be executed by krikri-playbook" where real ansible runs the plugin (ok=1, the plugin's marker written), and the plugin's own transport cannot be replayed in-process; recorded in a real-host round
1689	-k -K become prompt (issue repro)	needs an interactive prompt run: the [defaults to SSH password] suffix only shows under a pty, and real ansible's non-tty getpass fallback emits a Python traceback (GetPassWarning) no transcript match can pin machine-independently
1682	kpg host_key_checking config matrix	needs a real sshd whose host key is absent from (and then changed in) an isolated UserKnownHostsFile: the fresh-key refusal, the changed-key refusal and the vars>env>ini disabled-checking ladder only divide on a real dial, and a persisted ControlMaster masks every scenario after the first successful dial
1683	kpg sshd auth-failure repro	needs a real sshd: the rejected-key UNREACHABLE must embed ssh's whole stderr block (a warning line ahead of the Permission denied line), and the changed-host-key class/rc shape only exists against a live daemon whose key was swapped. The full-stderr detail extraction is covered in-process (test/integration/ssh_255_unreachable_test.cr's multi-line wrapper) and the bad-ansible_ssh_executable class/rc by the 1683-bad-ssh-executable corpus case
1673	sparknsh.graylog_collector	yum installs a release .rpm from a URL: the GPG failure only exists once a real dnf host downloads the unsigned rpm, and the CLI's transaction table names the @commandline nevra
1712	kpg yum_versionlock (state, happy path)	needs a real dnf host: yum's own versionlock plugin stamps a wall-clock "# Added lock on <ctime>" comment into /etc/dnf/plugins/versionlock.list, so the two engines' files can never hash alike (two real ansible runs disagree identically); the delegation krikri owns is pinned in-process by test/unit/yum_versionlock_test.cr
1729	ekultails.ansible_role_wine	real dnf install: the transaction-test file conflicts only exist once the host has openldap.x86_64 installed and the repo's openldap.i686 really conflicts with it; the shape krikri owns is pinned in-process by test/unit/dnf_install_failure_shape_test.cr
1747	kpg command env over ssh (PS1 from profile.d)	needs a real sshd on an RHEL-family host (Amazon Linux 2023/Rocky) whose /etc/profile.d exports PS1: only that bash SSH_SOURCE_BASHRC sourcing leaks PS1 into the persistent daemon, and no in-process local run reproduces the sshd-invoked bash
1755	kpg external plugin over ssh	external plugins need a real sshd: the per-platform upload (plugins-<key>/ chosen from the target's own uname), md5 de-duplication of a script plugin, the batch-script-vs-daemon split and PluginArchUnsupportedError for a target with no matching build are all transport decisions no in-process local run exercises
1759	kpg file (chaos: Typo on t0:command, WrongType on t1:path)	the only differing lines are the touch diff's wall-clock atime/mtime floats, which two runs of real ansible disagree on identically (KNOWN_MISSING's file state=touch entry); what krikri owns here - the integer path coerced to "5" and the four-key absent -> touch hunk under follow + modification_time_format - is pinned in-process by test/integration/touch_result_shape_test.cr
1785	kpg known_hosts (chaos: hash_host true)	no expected.out can pin this diff: the hash_host entry's |1|<salt>|<HMAC-SHA1> field is drawn afresh every run (real ansible salts it with os.urandom(20), so two runs of real ansible disagree identically) and it is the only differing line; what krikri owns - the field's fixed 28-character base64 width and that the digest is HMAC-SHA1 over the decoded salt and hostname - is pinned in-process by test/unit/known_hosts_key_test.cr
1789	crivetimihai.bootstrap	no expected.out can pin this diff: the role's raw `apt-get update && apt-get install -y python ...` needs a real root host with network, and on it apt repaints its progress meter once per tick, so the frame count and percentages follow that host's fetch timing - real ansible's own cold and warm runs disagree in exactly those chunks (cold downloaded noble-updates' InRelease plus its two Packages files, warm hit all four indexes with no `Fetched ... in Ns` line), leaving payload keys, rc=100, msg, changed, stderr and the `Package python is not available ...` tail identical; what krikri owns is pinned in-process by test/unit/task_executor_raw_pty_shape_test.cr (verbatim pty bytes, forwarded TERM, splitlines) and test/unit/ansible_splitlines_test.cr
1802	kpg subversion (state, happy path)	needs a real svn working copy (the suite has no svn): krikri's re-run must issue the same `svn status --quiet --ignore-externals`, `svn switch --revision <rev>` and `svn update -r <rev>` real ansible does even when the checkout is already at the target revision, and those commands' own rewrites of .svn/wc.db's stat cache are what makes the two hosts' state byte-identical. Proven on throwaway containers: with the same repository checked out, real ansible and krikri leave the same wc.db sha256 after both the first and the second run (that hash only compares across hosts when both check out the same repository: the fixtures create the repo - and so its random UUID - separately in each reference image, so the first run's wc.db hash can never match without a generator-side mask, per KNOWN_MISSING's wc.db entry; the two images' databases differ in nothing but that UUID)
1803	kpg multi-template (state, happy path)	no expected.out can pin this diff: the only differing state lines are ansible.builtin.tempfile's own mkstemp name under /tmp/kpg-work (prefix `kpg.`, suffix `.tmp`, eight random [a-z0-9_] characters between them), so two runs can never agree on it - the generator's --control run of real ansible on both hosts reproduces the same state:9b6901ec1080 signature, while stdout, stderr and the recap stay identical - and what krikri owns (the name's shape plus the on-disk 0600 mode and empty size the oracle's `f ... 0 0 600 0` and `e3b0c442...` lines report) is pinned in-process by test/integration/tempfile_test.cr
1804	kpg apt_repository (check mode, happy path)	no expected.out can pin this diff: its only content is real ansible's own `async_status: mode: cleanup` deleting the fixture's /root/.ansible_async/kpgjob - async_status.py declares check-mode support yet unlinks for mode=cleanup with no module.check_mode gate, so under --check both engines remove the file and the two deltas are byte-identical (the generator's --control run of real ansible on both hosts reports raw_identical stdout and still check_mode_mutated, the same check-mode:3bb5f161acaf signature). No krikri change can match or avoid it: a check-mode skip would break parity and leave the ansible-side delta alone in the oracle, and the oracle needs to prune ~/.ansible_async like ~/.ansible (KNOWN_MISSING's issue #1804 entry). What krikri owns - cleanup deleting the job file even with _ansible_check_mode set, returning ansible's ok/erased shape - is pinned in-process by test/unit/async_status_plugin_test.cr
1807	kpg file (check mode, happy path)	the only differing lines are the touch diff's wall-clock atime/mtime floats: the before pair is the file's pre-run stat (an atime only the container image owns, never moved by a write) and the after pair is one shared "now" read at each engine's run moment, which even two runs of real ansible never agree on (KNOWN_MISSING's file state=touch entry). The existing-path check-mode hunk's four keys, the file -> touch transition, the unchanged stat times and the `state: file` echo are pinned in-process by test/integration/touch_result_shape_test.cr
1809	kpg multi-gather_facts (check mode, happy path)	no expected.out can pin this diff: its only content is the async_wrapper job file a parallel gather leaves under --check (real ansible's gather_facts ACTION runs the fact module under async_wrapper when parallel: true, and the wrapper writes /root/.ansible_async/<jid>.<pid>, 0644, the whole facts payload, with or without --check - live-verified on ansible-core 2.21.6). krikri leaves the same artifact (issue #1808), so both deltas now carry one, but the random names and host-specific payloads still differ - the generator's --control run of real ansible on both hosts leaves two differently named/hashed files (9203 vs 9202 bytes) and still reports raw_identical stdout plus check_mode_mutated, the same state:9b6901ec1080 class, so no krikri change can match the random jid and content; the oracle needs to prune ~/.ansible_async like ~/.ansible (KNOWN_MISSING's issue #1808 entry). What krikri owns - the parallel gather's full fact payload (gather_subset plus module_setup) and one 0644 job file in the async dir, under --check too - is pinned in-process by test/integration/gather_facts_parallel_validation_test.cr
1808	kpg gather_facts (state, happy path)	no expected.out can pin this diff: its only content is the async_wrapper job file real ansible's parallel `gather_facts:` leaves behind (~/.ansible_async/j<random>.<pid>, 0644), whose name appends the pid of the process async_wrapper forked and whose payload is the host's own facts - two separately provisioned hosts can never agree on either (the generator's --control run of real ansible on both hosts leaves two such files itself - different names, 9195 and 9198 bytes, different hashes - and reports the same state:9b6901ec1080 signature, in check and real mode alike). What krikri owns - leaving the same job file, 0644 and named by the jid the rejected-argument form reports - is pinned in-process by test/unit/gather_facts_async_job_file_test.cr and replayed end to end by the 1808-gather-facts-parallel-job-file corpus case. The oracle needs to prune each home's async dir (~/.ansible_async, engine control-side state like the ~/.ansible staging root already pruned) before judging a state delta (KNOWN_MISSING's issue #1808 entry)
1812	kpg multi-tempfile-chaos (state, chaos: WrongType on t1:follow)	no expected.out can pin this diff: the only differing state lines are ansible.builtin.tempfile's own mkstemp name under /tmp/kpg-work (the module's default `ansible.` prefix plus eight random [a-z0-9_] characters), asked for with state: file and an already-existing path: directory, so both engines leave exactly one empty 0600 file there and never the same name; its stdout's raw differences (the `follow` conversion error's boolean literals in Python's per-run set-iteration order, and the `discovered_interpreter_python` fact real ansible attaches to the delegated failure) are both already masked. The generator's --control run of real ansible on both hosts leaves two differently named empty files and reports the same state:9b6901ec1080 signature, so no krikri change can match the name; what krikri owns - the name's shape plus the 0600 mode and empty size the oracle's `f ... 0 0 600 0` and `e3b0c442...` lines report - is pinned in-process by test/integration/tempfile_test.cr (KNOWN_MISSING's issue #1803 entry)
1814	kpg firewalld_info (check mode, happy path)	no expected.out can pin this diff: its only content is real ansible's own `Please note: zone:(...) have been ignored in the gathering process.` note, whose zone list comes from `list(set(specified_zones) - set(collected_zones))` in firewalld_info.py - Python string-hash randomization reorders it per module process, and repeated real `ansible-playbook` runs of the same task here alternated between `zone:(lnzequ,sujcww)` and `zone:(sujcww,lnzequ)`, so no krikri output can match every run. krikri keeps the declared order, one of real's possible outputs, and the generator needs a zone-list mask like FSTYPE-SET-ORDER (KNOWN_MISSING's firewalld_info entry). What krikri owns - the declared order in both the warning and undefined_zones - is pinned in-process by test/integration/firewalld_info_test.cr
1854	kpg cronvar (state, chaos: WrongType on t1:state)	no expected.out can pin this diff: the only differing state lines are the hash of /var/spool/cron/crontabs/root, whose content is the vixie `crontab` installer's own header - "# DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE..." then "# (/tmp/crontabXXXXXXXX installed on <wall clock>)" - so the staged name and the run moment differ by construction; the generator's --control run with real ansible on both hosts reports exactly the same hash-only state diff itself (the `file added f 0 997 600 194` line identical, both `hash added` values different). Both engines leave the same empty 194-byte 0600 root:crontab file (the task's insertbefore names a variable the empty crontab does not hold, which real cronvar drops while still reinstalling), which is what test/integration/cronvar_test.cr pins in-process: an emptied crontab staged as an empty file at Ansible's 20-character /tmp/crontabXXXXXXXX path, and a rendered one staged verbatim. The oracle needs to normalise the crontab header's path and timestamp before hashing that path (KNOWN_MISSING's issue #1854 entry)
1860	kpg multi-kernel_blacklist (check mode, happy path)	no expected.out can pin this diff: its only content is the empty /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-ansible.conf real ansible's own kernel_blacklist module creates under --check (kernel_blacklist.py's __init_module__ append-opens a missing blacklist_file before any check-mode gate, so the task reports changed and leaves a 0-byte file: live-verified on ansible-core 2.21.6 with a minimal connection: local playbook). Both engines' deltas are byte-identical (`file added f 0 0 644 0` plus `hash added e3b0c442...`) with stdout, stderr and the recap matching - the generator's --control run of real ansible on both hosts reports raw_identical: true and still check_mode_mutated: true with the same two-block diff, so no krikri change can silence it: a check-mode skip would break parity and leave the ansible-side delta alone in the oracle, which needs to treat a mutation both engines made identically as expected. What krikri owns - the created file's 0666 & ~umask mode (0644 under the reference umask 022, 0664 under 002) and the unchanged register surface under --check - is pinned in-process by test/integration/kernel_blacklist_test.cr (KNOWN_MISSING's issue #1860 entry)
1915	testing/lint/cases/noqa-legacy-tag	a krikri-lint divergence, not a playbook transcript: `# noqa: 301` is only a comment to ansible-playbook, so both engines print the same run for that task, and the difference exists only in ansible-lint's versus krikri-lint's lint report, which the corpus (a playbook-transcript replay) cannot express. The failure shape is pinned in-process by test/lint/config_noqa_test.cr and the fixture is re-linted against ansible-lint by testing/lint/parity.py
